subject: Action required: breach-notice trigger, transfer mechanics, and subprocessor access plan
messages:
From: Lauren Price <lprice@bluepeak.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: BluePeak Security Team <security@bluepeak.ai>
Date: 2028-05-15T08:15:12-07:00
Subject: Potential incident affecting BluePeak data stored by Redwood — initial notice

Hi Marcus,

I’m reaching out from BluePeak’s security team — we detected anomalous access patterns on May 14 affecting a subset of customer metadata that lives in your hosted environment for our account (account id BP-9142). At this point we are treating it as a potential confidentiality incident.

What we can share right now: a short summary of the indicators and a checksumed archive of aggregated security logs. We need to confirm the scope (which customer rows/objects were touched) and we may require a secure transfer of event logs and disk images for our forensics team.

Immediate asks:
- Please confirm whether Redwood considers this a reportable incident under our DPA clause 6.2 (notification within 72 hours).
- Provide the contact for privacy/evidence transfer and the preferred secure channel (SFTP, Airtight share, encrypted Drive).
- Identify any subprocessors that may have had access to the affected dataset in the last 30 days.

We are attaching a short log summary for triage (bluepeak_security_log_summary.pdf). We prefer to avoid broad escalation unless required; we value a coordinated handoff and will follow your evidence transfer checklist.

Thanks,
Lauren Price
Security Ops Manager
BluePeak Analytics
security@bluepeak.ai



---
Attachment: bluepeak_security_log_summary.pdf (application/pdf, 88 KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Price <lprice@bluepeak.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-15T09:03:41-07:00
Subject: Re: Potential incident affecting BluePeak data stored by Redwood — initial notice

Lauren — thanks for the head’s up and for the log summary. We are treating this as an incident report under the DPA and will start the notification workflow.

Quick plan / timeline:
- T0 (now): Acknowledge receipt and begin internal containment checks.
- T+24h: Initial scope estimate (which services, which datasets, approximate user counts).
- T+72h: Formal incident notification packet including evidence artifact list and required export/transfer steps.

Contacts:
- Privacy lead (cc’d): Neha Kapoor — will coordinate DPA obligations and evidence transfer.
- Legal/agreements: Monica Patel — for any contract redlines or urgent approvals.

Preferred evidence transfer: we can accept an encrypted bundle via our secure SFTP (credentials to be provisioned) or a signed DocuSign authorization to allow limited subprocessor access for forensics (template attached). If you send an encrypted archive, please include an SHA256 checksum and the key via a separate channel.

Regarding subprocessors: I’ll pull our access logs and list of active subprocessors against the BluePeak account and share within 24 hours. If you have a priority object list we should focus on, send it and we’ll target that in the initial scope.

I’m also looping in Rafael from infra (not included here to avoid broad cc) to run a deeper memory/DKIM check.

Onboarding next steps below — we’ll avoid unnecessary data movement until we agree the minimal set.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Price <lprice@bluepeak.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-15T11:27:05-07:00
Subject: Re: Potential incident affecting BluePeak data stored by Redwood — initial notice

Hi all — looping in a few legal/privacy pointers we need to lock before any evidence handoff. Short answers up front: yes, this triggers the 72-hour notification obligation under our DPA language if we confirm unauthorized access; and we must verify subprocessors and transfer safeguards before moving customer content cross-border.

Please note the following requirements from our side:
- Evidence transfer authorization: BluePeak must execute our limited-scope transfer authorization (attached) or provide a signed equivalent. Template: transfer_authorization_template.docx.
- Allowed subprocessors: We will provide the list of subprocessors who had technical access within the last 30 days. If any of your forensics partners require direct access, we need a written statement and minimal access window; Redwoods’ standard is approval + signed MOU.
- Data minimization: only the minimum logs/artifacts relevant for forensics should be transferred. Avoid full account exports unless explicitly necessary.
- Cross-border transfers: if artifacts include EU personal data, we will route through our EU transfer bucket only; otherwise we may need SCCs or customer consent depending on destination.

Action items for BluePeak: please review and sign the transfer template or confirm your alternate process. Once signed, we’ll provision SFTP credentials and initiate a secure intake flow.

Links: DocuSign sign request (https://www.docusign.com/en/link/example-signature-request) and our incident ticket (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-789).

Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Cc: Lauren Price <lprice@bluepeak.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T11:02:05-07:00
Subject: Re: Potential incident affecting BluePeak data stored by Redwood — initial notice

Marcus / Monica — thanks for the quick responses. We agree to the limited-scope transfer flow and will sign the transfer authorization. We are attaching: a short consolidated log summary (bluepeak_security_log_summary.pdf) and an encrypted disk image placeholder (preserved_disk_image.tar.enc).

Plan we propose:
1) BluePeak signs and returns the transfer_authorization_template.docx via DocuSign by EOD today.
2) Redwood provisions SFTP creds and provides an intake path; BluePeak will push encrypted artifacts and post the SHA256 hash in a separate email.
3) Redwood sends a list of subprocessors with access and timestamps for the last 30 days (we need names and the role that provided access).

We agree to the data minimization request — we’ll only send the artifacts required for immediate triage. We will also notify any of our contracted forensics partners that they must execute Redwood’s MOU before any direct access.

Appreciate the coordinated approach. Please confirm the SFTP hostname and the contact who will validate checksums once the upload completes.

Thanks,
Anu Verma
Head of Incident Response
BluePeak Analytics
anu.verma@bluepeak.ai
